revised_hypotheses: Belinostat is a hydroxamic acid HDAC inhibitor; its A375 anchor profile is dominated by increased H3K18ac1K23ac1 and H3K9ac1K14ac1 with decreased H3K9me2K14ac0, H3K9me1K14ac0, H3K9me3K14ac0, and H3K27me0K36me2, consistent with a histone acetylation/repressive-methylation perturbation.
RGFP966 (HDAC3-selective inhibitor) had the highest anchor similarity (0.5657) and structure similarity (0.3) among candidates, but no retrieved source supports its donor response.

Decitabine is a 2'-deoxyribonucleoside (pubchem:451668:description:1) and bortezomib is a reversible 26S proteasome inhibitor (pubchem:387447:description:1); neither retrieved description supports a belinostat-like histone acetylation donor response.

The fixed decoder selects a target cell/feature/sign; the ridge diagnostic (PC3, BI10036, H3K27me1K36me1, sign -1) and phenotype/chemical diagnostics (MCF7, BI10031, H3K18ac1K23ac1, sign +1) suggest the transfer may be driven by H3K18ac1K23ac1 gain and H3K27me1K36me1 loss.
unresolved: No retrieved source provides measured donor target-minus-A375 responses or histone perturbation values for any candidate donor.
No retrieved source supports RGFP966, tacrolimus, geldanamycin, or other candidates as donors for the belinostat anchor profile.
The >0.5 log2 histone perturbation versus vehicle cannot be verified from the supplied pharmacology descriptions alone.
